title: tracy-web: a brief settled after a restart and the /ops Website opportunities queue judge database-written times on one clock, so an app clock ahead of PostgreSQL no longer marks a live shared worker's lease expired or drops interruptedAt
steps: S1: With TEST_DATABASE_URL set, from the checkout run: node --import ./scripts/clock-shift.mjs --test --test-reporter=tap apps/tracy-web/test/brief-build.test.mjs apps/tracy-web/test/ops-wo-shared-research.test.mjs (the preload moves the JavaScript clock 400 days ahead; PostgreSQL stays on the real clock).
S2: Record the exit code and the result of the cases named in run.tests.
expect: S1 exits 0 with "# fail 0" and "# skipped 0".
A brief that a starting process settles carries timings.interruptedAt from the build module's own clock (the same clock as its other writers and its reader), within the last minute of Date.now().

/ops lists a shared worker whose lease_until is an hour after the database's now() as collecting ("Collecting website (2/3 done)"), not "Worker lease expired on shared-worker", although Date.now() is past lease_until.
The live duration of a running research job is measured on the database clock: 120 to 129 seconds for a job created two minutes earlier by now().

selectors.brief: apps/tracy-web/src/sites/brief-build.js (recoverLost: interruptedAt bound as $7 from now())
selectors.ops: apps/tracy-web/src/lib/wo-ops.js (jobClock, db_now in the listWoQueue job query)

evidence: 17/11/2026 release PR develop→main, job "build check (checks)", step "Tests with the clock moved forward" (scripts/run-clock-shift.mjs): brief-build.test.mjs:1048 failed Number(prep.timings.interruptedAt) > Date.now() - 60_000; ops-wo-shared-research.test.mjs:75/118/125 got 'Worker lease expired on shared-worker' instead of 'Collecting website (2/3 done)' and a durationSec outside 120..129. Both files were green on the real clock: the product compared PostgreSQL now()/clock_timestamp() times with JavaScript Date.now().
fence: The shifted-clock preload stands in for an application clock that drifts ahead of the database; the real PostgreSQL writes every fixture time with now().
